title: Grade 11 Physics - Kinematics: Motion in One Dimension
subject: Physics

transcript.text: Welcome to kinematics — the study of motion. We describe motion using four key quantities: position, displacement, velocity, and acceleration.

Displacement is the change in position. It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction. If you walk 5 m east then 3 m west, your displacement is 2 m east, even though you travelled 8 m total.
Average velocity is displacement divided by time. It differs from speed because velocity is a vector. If displacement is 30 m north over 6 seconds, average velocity is 5 m/s north.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. If a car speeds up from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 seconds, its acceleration is (30 - 10) / 5 = 4 m/s squared.

The kinematic equations relate displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time for uniform acceleration. The most useful is: s = ut + (1/2)at squared, where s is displacement, u is initial velocity, a is acceleration, and t is time.

Free fall is a classic application. Near Earth's surface, all objects fall with the same acceleration: g = 9.8 m/s squared downward, ignoring air resistance. If you drop an object from rest, after 3 seconds its velocity is 9.8 times 3 = 29.4 m/s downward.

Graphical analysis is powerful. A position-time graph's slope gives velocity. A velocity-time graph's slope gives acceleration, and its area gives displacement. These graphical relationships connect directly to the kinematic equations.

interventions.question: A student walks 5 m east then 3 m west. What is the student's total displacement?
interventions.correct_feedback: Correct! Displacement = final position - initial position = 5 - 3 = 2 m east.
interventions.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. Displacement is the net change in position: 5 m east minus 3 m west = 2 m east.

interventions.question: If displacement is 30 m north in 6 seconds, what is average velocity?
interventions.correct_feedback: Correct! Velocity = displacement / time = 30 / 6 = 5 m/s north.
interventions.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. Average velocity = displacement / time. 30 m / 6 s = 5 m/s north.

interventions.question: A car accelerates from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 seconds. What is the acceleration?
interventions.incorrect_feedback: Not quite. Acceleration = change in velocity / time = (30 - 10) / 5 = 4 m/s².
